extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and law students studying patent validity and infringement defenses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for determining when prior use, sale, disclosure, secrecy, delay, or breach of confidence constitute a public use, sale, or abandonment that defeats novelty or invalidates a subsequent patent. Focused on evidence, intent, statutory limits (act of 1839), and the experimental-use/confidentiality exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption_of_acquiescence_public_use
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the presumption of acquiescence in public use arises may turn materially on whether the inventor used the invention himself, or imparted knowledge of it to others, with or without an intention to limit such use or knowledge in respect to time, extent, or object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court will examine inventor's conduct and intent as a material element; public use presumption arises where public use is known or might be known to the inventor and no limiting intent is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental_use_exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of the invention by the inventor himself, for purposes of experiment or completion, before taking out a patent, does not give rise to the inference that he intends to surrender his invention to the public; experimental practice, even in public, will not alone prove dedication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary or occasional uses (e.g., a few persons, acts of accommodation, short and limited periods) are not public uses. The public use must be generally allowed or unlimited in time, extent, or object to defeat the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No_public_use_if_evidence_shows_no_intent_for_gain
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general test, where evidence stops short of proving such a use, exercise, or practice for the purpose of gain, a 'public use' will not be proved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts look for use for profit or other indicia of commercialization; mere operation or trial without profit motive or without uncontrolled dissemination is insufficient to establish public use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful_experiment_with_profit_not_necessarily_publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An experiment performed in the presence of others which not only turns out successful but actually benefits the inventor in that instance is not necessarily a publication or gift of the invention to the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether decisive experiments remain to be made (scale, environment), whether profit was incidental/coincident, and whether the inventor applied for a patent with reasonable expedition; repeated use or unnecessary delay after successful experiments may change the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere_delay_or_forbearance_no_presumption_of_abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere forbearance on the part of an inventor to apply for a patent during the progress of experiments and until he has perfected his invention and tested its value affords no just grounds for presuming abandonment or dedication to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay alone is immaterial except insofar as it tends to show acquiescence in any public use that occurred or that the inventor's acts went beyond experimental/limited permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral_disclosure_and_silence_not_estoppel_without_harm
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a patentee explained his invention orally to several persons, without written specification or model, and that another later described and perfected the same thing in the patentee's presence, and the patentee made no claim, does not bar an infringement action; silence works no estoppel unless it has misled another to his injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts require evidence that silence actually misled and caused injury before applying estoppel against the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential_manufacture_and_secrecy_injunction_not_public_use
rubrics_metrics.description: Making a single specimen (or manufacturing under the direction of the patentee) under an injunction of secrecy, kept from public view and shipped abroad, is not a 'public use' within the realm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy, confidentiality, and the context (e.g., made for foreign use or under confidentiality for a prospective assignee/participant) support a finding that the act was private rather than public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale_to_single_person_may_be_public_use_pre-1839
rubrics_metrics.description: Under earlier law, the sale of even a single specimen of an invention to a purchaser who might choose to buy could amount to a public use or sale and defeat a subsequent patent (because it could be treated as an article of commerce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule was seen as creating inconvenience (possible effective extension of monopoly) and was addressed by later legislation (act of 1839). Courts consider whether the sale was essentially a commercial public sale or a private/confidential transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act_of_1839_prior_use_protection_and_two-year_limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of 1839 provides that a person who purchased or constructed a newly invented machine, manufacture, or composition prior to the inventor's patent application may use and vend the specific thing without liability, and such prior purchase, sale, or use shall not invalidate the patent except on proof of abandonment to the public or that the prior use was for more than two years prior to application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statute affords a safe harbor for prior private sales/uses to individuals but preserves invalidity where abandonment is proved or the prior use/sale continued beyond two years before application; courts construe 'newly invented...' broadly to mean the invention whatever its subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited_permission_to_others_does_not_invalidate_if_control_maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee allowed limited uses to others (for purposes other than experiment or completion) — e.g., neighborly kindness or accommodation — and the use was clearly limited and under the inventor's control with a manifested intention to retain exclusive rights, such use will not operate to invalidate the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key factors are limitation of purpose, absence of profit motive, and preservation of control and intention to reserve rights; evidence must exclude that the patentee put the thing into public use for profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach_of_confidence_publication_not_consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention comes into public use through a breach of confidence by a person who received it confidentially, that public use is not 'with the consent or allowance' of the patentee; if the patentee takes immediate steps to give notice of his exclusive right, he may still obtain a valid patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute's language and cases distinguish public use with consent from use arising from misuse of confidential information; prompt action by inventor is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent_to_abandon_requires_clear_manifestation_of_conduct_or_declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: To constitute abandonment to the public that will destroy the right to a patent, the inventor must have intended to give up and relinquish his right, as evinced by declarations, conduct, or omissions; mere use without such intent may be insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juries are to be instructed to examine plaintiff's declarations, conduct, and omissions and the justice/integrity of defendants' conduct; intent may be found from pattern of behavior, statements, or manifest accommodations to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior_purchase_sale_or_use_not_per_se_abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: A particular purchase, sale, or prior use before application does not of itself constitute abandonment to the public; it will not invalidate per se unless connected with other facts showing abandonment or unless it has continued more than two years prior to application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proving abandonment usually requires evidence dehors the mere transaction — patterns, duration, profit motive, publicity, or other surrounding circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter_scope_and_specific_thing_limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute's phrase 'newly invented machine, manufacture, or composition of matter' is construed to mean the invention patented, whatever its subject-matter (including processes), and the purchaser's authorized use refers to the specific thing as originally invented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts interpret the purchaser's right as limited to the specific article purchased; the protection extends to the invention's subject-matter generally but is bounded by what was actually acquired and used.
